title: Deep neural networks to map the pace of brain aging before Alzheimer's disease
text:
This project aims to develop deep learning models for estimating local brain age (LBA) and the pace of brain
aging (PBA) from MRI, providing more precise and dynamic biomarkers of neurodegeneration. Using large da-
tasets, we will train neural networks to map LBA and PBA across the brain, integrate generative AI to forecast
future brain aging trajectories, and apply deep survival models to improve Alzheimer’s disease (AD) risk stratifi-
cation. By advancing brain age estimation methods, this research will enhance early detection of AD risk, inform
clinical monitoring strategies, and support personalized interventions to slow neurodegeneration.

title: Comparative systems biology of apicomplexan cell division
text:
Apicomplexan parasites have major impacts on human health e.g. Plasmodium falciparum causes malaria whereas
Toxoplasma gondii and Babesia spp. cause opportunistic infections. At the heart of all apicomplexan pathogenesis lies
cell division, which unfolds in seemingly diverse and exotic ways, and is one of the defining features of the Apicomplexa.
The dramatic phenomenological difference from the standard mammalian cell division model is pursued here in a
opportunistic survey for urgently needed new and specific drugs to treat malaria, toxoplasmosis, and emerging tick-
transmitted babesiosis.

title: Streamlined development of an IND with the silica nanocapsule loaded with Cas9 genome editors to disrupt the dominant BEST1 mutant allele
text: PROJECT SUMMARY– FOLLOWER PROJECT 3. Best Vitelliform Macular Dystrophy, or Best disease (BD), is a relatively common inherited macular degenerative disorder that results in retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) dysfunction and progressive loss of central vision. BD is caused by over 200 different missense mutations in the BEST1 gene. Currently, there are no treatments for autosomal dominant BD due in part to the absence of relevant animal models. To overcome the difficulties in modeling the effects of many pathogenic BEST1 mutations, we utilize patient-specific iPSC-RPE models to develop a biological system that can rapidly screen genome editing leads. As in Follower Project 2, we hypothesize that Cas9-mediated indel formation by the leads in the mutant BEST1 allele will cause frameshifts leading to premature stop codons and resulting in nonsense- mediated decay of the edited transcript, removing the dominant-negative effect and restoring function to the wild- type allele. Our objective in Project 3 is to develop an SNC product, SNC-201, containing a Cas9 payload to specifically target BEST1 mutant alleles and compare various approaches using ribonucleoproteins (RNPs) and Cas9 mRNA/sgRNAs. To achieve this, we will pursue four aims. First, we will generate dual BEST1 allele BD iPSC-RPE reporter systems to facilitate on/off-target analysis of mutant allele targeting. We have developed a BD dual reporter iPSC line that has the mutant BEST1 allele linked to a 3’ tdTomato reporter and the wild-type BEST1 allele linked to a 3’ GFP reporter. Via fluorescent imaging, we can monitor the expression of both the targeted mutant BEST1 allele and the wild-type allele, which is the top ‘off-target’ site for our strategy. Plus, we can monitor channel function on sorted cells. We will adapt this reporter iPSC line to create a wild-type and eight additional mutant lines. Second, we compare the modular editor components of the lead SNC-201s. Using the dual reporter systems transfected with SNC formulations containing RNPs or Cas9 mRNA/sgRNA, we will rapidly screen SNC formulations to disrupt each mutant allele in dual reporter iPSC-RPEs. A comparison of the editing efficiency of Cas9 mRNA/sgRNA and RNP will be achieved through this work. Third, we scale up the synthesis of the SNC RNP leads and rely on Lead Project 1 for protocols to scale up mRNA/sgRNA leads. Finally, we generate a preclinical package for SNC-201 targeting selected mutant BEST1 alleles. After evaluating the safety of an SNC-201 formulation in nonhuman primates, we will complete one INTERACT meeting with the FDA for a product that intends to treat BD patients with multiple different mutations. After obtaining feedback, we will draft a clinical development plan for a pre-IND meeting. Successful completion of our aims will provide a rigorous, stepwise approach to developing an IND for targeting specific mutations – a strategy that could be expanded for all individuals with BD – and address central questions pertaining to the application of gene editing for genotypically heterogeneous dominant diseases. It will also advance the utility of iPSC models as custom preclinical tools to rapidly develop somatic cell genome editing strategies.

title: Regulation and Function of Viral and Endogenous Circular RNA in Cancer
text:
Circular ribonucleic acid (circRNA) molecules are enriched in head and neck squamous cell carcinomas
(HNSCC) but their potential functions remain unclear. Through our study of human papillomavirus (HPV)
circRNAs, we have developed novel approaches and tools to study circular RNA in HNSCC. This study will
advance our understanding of HNSCC biology and may also identify new prognostic biomarkers and
treatment approaches for HNSCC.

title: Imaging and Genomic Signatures of Brain Tumor Heterogeneity and Evolution to Optimize Patient Management
text:
OVERALL: PROJECT NARRATIVE
The overall goal of this renewal P01 proposal is to identify imaging and genomic signatures of brain tumor
heterogeneity and evolution to optimize patient management of the two most common primary brain tumors in
adults: glioblastoma and meningioma. This will be achieved by integrating multi-parametric imaging strategies
assessing spatial and temporal changes in individual patients during the course of their disease along with
genomic properties of the tumor. We will ascertain non-invasive imaging markers that reflect the underlying
biological mechanisms driving glioblastoma evolution and mengingioma molecular differentiation to improve
patient care through informing new therapeutic targets and ways to monitor early response.

title: SCH: Simulation Optimization of Cardiac Surgical Planning
text:
This project is relevant to the mission of the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute because it will drive
cardiac modeling and simulation into clinical applications, promote data-driven and simulation-guided
surgical planning, and develop an interdisciplinary workforce who possesses both computational skills
and medical insights. The success of this project will make a lasting impact on our society and bring a
heart-healthy future.

title: PRECISE (PeRfusion imaging to identify postErior CIrculation candidateS for thrombectomy)
text:
PROJECT NARRATIVE .
Acute ischemic stroke caused by occlusion of the vertebral or basilar arteries is a devastating disease that
results in high rates of death and disability. Patients with vertebral or basilar artery occlusions often undergo
endovascular thrombectomy treatment to restore blood flow in these vessels, which is thought to improve the
chances of a good outcome in these patients. The goal of PRECISE is to determine if advanced cerebral
perfusion imaging can identify a subset of patients with vertebral or basilar artery occlusion who are more likely
to benefit from endovascular thrombectomy. The results of PRECISE will improve our ability to identify patients
for emergency thrombectomy and may lead to improved patient selection and prognostication in this
understudied stroke population.

title: Association of Stigmatizing EHR Language with Clinician-Patient Communication and Patient Experience
text:
This administrative supplement to the parent grant will support the career of Amanda McArthur,
PhD, who comes from a background underrepresented in science. Further, the project Dr.
McArthur undertakes will provide data about how stigmatizing documentation relates to observed
interpersonal processes and patient experience of care. The project proposed here could provide
compelling evidence of the need for change in the ways we document about patients.

title: Creating tools to make experimental biochemistry accessible to people with blindness
text:
The imagery, data and experimental tools of biomedical science are
inaccessible to people with blindness, leading to systemic exclusion. This proposal is
utilizing universal design to create and test new technology to make data and laboratory
tools of molecular science accessible to lab members with blindness (and other people
with blindness). The tools will then be used by sighted and blind members of the PI’s lab
to test biomedical hypotheses in bioinorganic and biophysical chemistry.

title: Hematopoietic stem cell encoded anti-tumor immunity: mechanisms and function
text:
This project investigates the immune mechanisms that underlie the success of the oldest immunotherapy of
cancer, the bacterium BCG. By understanding how BCG unleashes the immune system against bladder
cancer, we hope to predict who will respond to BCG and to learn broader lessons about immunotherapies that
can be applied to other cancers and therapies.

title: Precision Diagnostics in T-cell Mediated Rejection: Predicting Treatment Resistance at Time of Diagnosis
text:
T-cell mediated rejection (TCMR) is the leading cause of kidney transplant failure, with treatment requiring
aggressive immunosuppression. With only a fraction of TCMR patients responsive to therapy, an urgent need
exists for a means of identifying patients likely to be treatment resistant. The PI, Dr. Coley, has worked for years
to identify a panel of genes differentially expressed in treatment resistant versus sensitive TCMR patients, and
here, we will develop a commercializable assay to guide treatment decisions in these fragile patients.

title: Summer Institute in Neuroimaging and Data Science
text:
Summer Institute in Neuroimaging and Data Science: Project Narrative
The Summer Institute in Neuroimaging and Data Science (“NeuroHackademy”) provides training in state-of-the-
art data science methods and resources, such as programming, data stewardship, and machine learning, that
are underrepresented in traditional neuroscience curricula. Through lectures, hands-on training sessions, and
team projects, the skills taught by the SINDS will empower scientists from diverse backgrounds to use these tools
in research on the human brain and on neurological and psychiatric brain disorders.

title: Acquisition-independent machine learning for morphometric analysis of underrepresented aging populations with clinical and low-field brain MRI
text:
Brain MRI scans in the clinic (both with high-field scanners and low-field
portable scanners) and in research are very different, as the former consist of a small set of
widely spaced slices, whereas the latter have more slices, closer together. Aging and
Alzheimer’s research on the human brain with MRI currently relies on computer software
that requires scans like those used in research and does not work with clinical or low-field
scans. We propose to create and distribute tools that use artificial intelligence to make
clinical and low-field scans usable by research software, thus enabling researchers
worldwide to study aging and Alzheimer’s in: (i) broader clinical populations that are
present in substantial numbers among the millions of scans already stored in hospitals;
and (ii) populations in rural areas that may be reached with low-cost, portable scanners.

title: Plasma membrane stress response
text:
Many eukaryotic cells undergo rapid changes in shape or size, which changes the cell surface
area. To accommodate these changes, cells fuse the cell surface to internal membrane structures
to allow for the rapid exchange of membranes. This mechanism seems to play an important role
not only to avoid cell rupture but also in the function of many human cells, including blood platelets
and neuronal development.

title: Effect of Extracellular Citrate on Neuronal Excitability in SLC13A5 Epilepsy
text:
SLC13A5 Epilepsy is a rare genetic epilepsy caused by mutations in the SLC13A5 citrate
transporter protein. Elevated citrate levels have been observed in these patients, but the effect
of citrate on the nervous system are not well understood. I will use mouse models to investigate
the relationship between citrate levels and brain excitability to improve our understanding of
SLC13A5 Epilepsy and its underlying mechanisms.

title: Aldosterone-Vascular Signaling on Cerebral Small Vessel Function
text:
Cerebral small vessel dysfunction is a major contributor to vascular cognitive impairment. Based on our
compelling preliminary evidence, this project aims to determine the blood pressure-independent mechanisms
underlying deterioration of cortical and subcortical small vessel function by excess plasma aldosterone
(hyperaldosteronemia) and subsequent activation of mineralocorticoid receptors—the cognate receptors for
aldosterone.

title: CSHL Conference on Germ Cells (2026-2030)
text:
Animals and plants are composed of somatic cells, that form the body, and germ cells, that transmit genetic
material to the next generation through the union of egg and sperm. This international conference will
highlight the latest advances in germline biology in a range of organisms and experimental systems. By
emphasizing emerging topics in germline specification, the development of germ cells, gamete formation,
fertilization and egg to embryo transition, the meeting will offer valuable opportunities to share discoveries
and for foster collaborations. The insights presented are expected to advance our understanding of gene
transmission and reproduction with important implications for human health.

title: Potent broadly neutralizing antibody development against the HIV-1 fusion peptide epitope
text:
The fusion peptide of HIV-1 is a vulnerable target site with tremendous promise for new preventions and
treatments. This project applies recently established technologies to understand how antibodies against the
fusion peptide effectively suppress HIV-1. This study will reveal new best-in-class antibody drugs against the
fusion peptide site and provide actionable vaccine strategies to help end the HIV-1 pandemic.

title: Synaptic organization of cholinergic interneurons in the nucleus accumbens
text:
The nucleus accumbens (NAc) is part of the ventral striatum, plays a key role in motivated behaviors, and is
disrupted in substance use disorder. Here we use advanced anatomy, electrophysiology, and optogenetics to
examine the long-range and local inputs onto cholinergic interneurons (CINs) in the mouse NAc core
(NAcCore). Our experiments will further our understanding of how different types of glutamatergic and
GABAergic inputs both contact and influence the firing properties of CINs in this important brain circuit.

title: Dissecting neocortical field potential dynamics using optical voltage imaging in genetically targeted cell-types
text: Recordings of cortical field potentials are widely used in basic and clinical neuroscience and include electroencephalography (EEG), electrocorticography (ECoG) and local field potential (LFP) recordings, which all provide time-varying voltage signals reflecting neural population activity. However, the neural origins of field potential dynamics remain poorly understood, due to a lack of techniques for dissecting how different classes of cells contribute to field potential signals. To break this longstanding impasse, our project applies recently developed voltage-indicators and optical instrumentation for imaging the transmembrane voltage dynamics of genetically defined neuron classes; these techniques will enable us to systematically identify the contributions of 12 different cell- types to neocortical field potential activity.
